hypothesis: input-induced state transitions reach a modifying component without the validator holding write authority

W1_deferred_write.LABEL: callback-mediated trigger / parser-native adoption: the parser's documented adoption of hook returns (PyDict result replaced at scan_once epilogue) determines WHICH value Component C commits; the write itself is application code.
W1_deferred_write.falsifier: commit shows 'safe' => hook return was not adopted downstream

W2_semantic_write.LABEL: semantic write: input bytes unchanged; caller-configured decode policy changed how Component C interprets existing information.
W2_semantic_write.caveat: requires two consumers with DIFFERENT policies wired to the same signed bytes to escalate beyond configuration divergence.

W3_preverdict_mutation.LABEL: construction/validation fusion consequence (documented behaviour): an operation outside the validator observes state written by a hook even though the document never passed validation.

W4_resource_retention.LABEL: resource-retention effect: input SHAPE (where corruption sits) determines whether the full authenticated buffer stays reachable; retention itself is the documented exception interface, the LEVERAGE is that a remote byte pattern controls another component's memory lifetime.
W4_resource_retention.falsifier: weakref dead while exception alive => exc.doc does not retain the buffer

W5_gc_finalizer_path.LABEL: the __del__ that fired belongs to an object THIS TEST created. Parser-allocated dicts/lists/strs carry no user finalizers, so no evidence that parse-time allocation churn causes another component's finalizer to run with parse-controlled timing. Path left open only for caller-attached proxies, which is callback-mediated by definition.

W6_lifecycle_control.LABEL: input shape chooses WHICH failure mode propagates to the error handler (Component C of this path); handlers classically perform different state transitions per exception type (log level, response class, retry semantics). Note depth_950_C accepted on this build — C scanner budget differs from py, consistent with rev2 divergence.
